text:
alice: FYI — found ~12 debug logs in priv-s3 when quota fallback rerouted requests yesterday. Bodies included user prompts. :grimacing:
ben: oh no. any pattern? route/tenant?
alice: all from the canary route 'fast-path' during a burst. looks like fallback went to 'deep-inspect' which is allowed to capture full req/resp for oncall, but tenant opt-out wasn't honored.
claire: That's bad. Is this the reroute rule that uses 'force_debug=true' sketch?
alice: here's the policy snippet I pulled from the decision logs:
```
- when: quota_exceeded AND env == prod
  action: reroute
  to: deep-inspect
  meta:
    capture: full_body
    tenant_override: false
```
dan: we intentionally set tenant_override:false for privacy — suggests the check isn't running. @ops-bot did any manual reroute happen during the outage?
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Routing policy v2.3.1 deployed 2024-05-17T03:12Z to prod. No manual reroute events in audit log.
eva: I suspect the sampler later in the pipeline applied an old allowlist. If deep-inspect downstream assumes bodies are scrubbed, it might rehydrate. can we confirm sanitizer ran?
ben: quick mitigation idea: add a required flag on reroute decisions so downstream rejects raw_bodies unless privacy_check=true. minimal patch to policy layer.
claire: agree. also we should surface when fallback routes increase retention TTL — add a console flag/toast 'Fallback route: high-retention' in telemetry.
alice: proposed patch: enforce tenant consent at routing decision, never attach raw body to reroute event (attach body_reference), and emit metric `reroute_privacy_check_failed`.
dan: low-risk. can we hotfix to prod? need to rotate S3 access and run purge job too.
eva: i'll open a runbook: revoke deep-inspect s3 read perms, purge the objects, and notify legal. also add console guard that marks "can capture" routes in orange.
ben: one API debate: should routing policy be allowed to mutate requests (strip PII) or only instruct downstream scrubbing? incident favors mutation at decision-time.
claire: vote for explicit mutation at policy layer with an auditable transform log. downstream should not be trusted to scrub.
alice: i'll open two PRs: (A) enforcement + body_reference change (hotfix) — ETA 2h, (B) policy-transform API prototype. will @everyone on the PR.
ops-bot: incident-bot: incident created #incident-2024-05-17-reroute-leak (P0).
ben: :thumbsup:
